page: Amazon Web Services m7i.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a custom fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processor (model 8488C) operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 32 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Network performance is provisioned with a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for persistent block storage.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate competitive single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2030 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2700, both landing in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Multi-core compute performance remains consistent across standard workloads, recording 7317.45 in stress-ng multi-core and 7729.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Cryptographic acceleration and vectorized operations benefit from integrated instruction sets including AES-NI, AVX-512, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth measures 579.72 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and roughly 50 GB/sec for uncached read and write passes, supporting 10.81 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.35 GB/sec of static web throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge primarily in heavily threaded, throughput-bound operations and local I/O dependencies. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and continuous 7B parameter LLM text generation fall into lower-tier performance bands due to the 4-core physical CPU limit and lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The absence of integrated NVMe drives also means I/O-heavy applications must account for network storage latency. Nonetheless, the balanced resource allocation and fast DDR5 memory yield reliable compute-to-memory density for general enterprise workloads, application servers, microservices, mid-sized databases, and continuous integration environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz, alongside 32 GB of DDR5 memory. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the instance offers a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It includes no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on external EBS volumes for storage persistence. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core performance and text processing capabilities, supported by steady multi-core execution and memory throughput reaching 50.51 GB/sec on uncached reads. Tradeoffs include modest multi-threaded decompression efficiency and lower token generation speeds on medium language models. The instance is well-matched for enterprise application servers, mid-tier relational databases, static web delivery, and CI/CD pipelines.
